Technically yes, but the rules file lists the identifier as permanent, so changing it means deliberately retiring that invariant. As the owner, you can make that call. I can't see `docs/release.md` or `AGENTS.md` here, so I'm going only on the excerpt.

**The deciding question is whether any build with `is.waiwai.dictation` is already on someone else's Mac** (beta testers, early users, a published appcast).

- **If no one outside your own machines has it:** the rename is cheap. You'd re-grant Accessibility on your own devices and that's it.
- **If anyone has it installed:**
  - macOS treats the new identifier as a different app, so they lose the Accessibility grant and have to re-approve it.
  - Sparkle generally refuses to update an app into a bundle with a different identifier. Those users likely can't auto-update and would need a manual download of the new app.
  - Anything keyed to the old identifier (UserDefaults domain, Application Support folder, Keychain items) won't carry over without a migration.

**If you go ahead:**
- Keep the existing Sparkle EdDSA key. The rename doesn't affect it, and the "never generate a replacement" rule still stands.
- Keep signing Sparkle nested code inside out, with no `codesign --deep`.
- Update the invariant in the rules file, `docs/release.md`, and `AGENTS.md`. Otherwise future agents and contributors will treat the new identifier as forbidden to change, or revert the rename as a violation.
- Search the project for every use of the old identifier (Info.plist, entitlements, build settings, appcast, helper bundles, URL schemes, etc.).

My recommendation: if the app has truly never shipped to outside users, rename now, since this is the cheapest moment. If it has, keep `is.waiwai.dictation` and put the new name in the display name instead.
